evidenceAudit.scope: Seizures in newborns in India: recognition, immediate correction of hypoglycaemia and hypocalcaemia, anticonvulsant sequence, investigations for the cause, duration of treatment and follow-up, built on the ICMR Neonatal Seizures STW (July 2020).
findings: Seizure types, glucose below 45 mg/dL treated with 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg then 6 mg/kg/min, 10% calcium gluconate 2 mL/kg diluted 1:1 over 10 minutes with cardiac monitoring, phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg then 10 mg/kg, phenytoin 20 mg/kg PE, lorazepam 0.05 mg/kg, midazolam bolus and infusion to 18 µg/kg/min, levetiracetam 40 mg/kg then 40–60 mg/kg/day, maintenance rules, investigations and stopping rules checked against the ICMR Neonatal Seizures STW (July 2020).
unverifiedSections: The ICMR workflow does not rank lorazepam, midazolam and levetiracetam after phenytoin; the order in the workflow is followed.
Maintenance doses are not given in the workflow.
Magnesium and pyridoxine are not covered in the workflow.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Seizures in newborns are often subtle — lip smacking, cycling movements, eye deviation, apnoea or heart-rate changes — and frequently reflect serious illness: hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy, hypoglycaemia, hypocalcaemia, sepsis or meningitis, intracranial haemorrhage, or congenital infection. The ICMR workflow first secures temperature, airway, breathing and circulation, then corrects low glucose and calcium, then gives phenobarbitone and further drugs in sequence, while investigating the cause. Most babies need only short treatment; long-term neurodevelopmental and hearing follow-up is essential.
keyMechanisms: The immature brain is excitable because GABA can be excitatory in early life.
Hypoxia-ischaemia, hypoglycaemia and hypocalcaemia lower the seizure threshold.
Infection and haemorrhage injure the cortex directly.

physicalSigns: Rhythmic jerks of limbs or face; tonic posturing (ICMR STW)
Pedalling, rowing or swimming movements; lip pouting or sucking (ICMR STW)
Vacant stare, eye deviation, repeated blinking (ICMR STW)
Apnoea, heart rate or BP fluctuation (ICMR STW)
redFlags: Bulging fontanelle or bleeding tendency (intracranial bleed)

clinicalManagement.title: Stabilise
actions: Temperature, airway, breathing, circulation; IV access (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Correct glucose and calcium
actions: Glucose below 45 mg/dL: 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg, then 6 mg/kg/min (ICMR STW).
10% calcium gluconate 2 mL/kg diluted 1:1 over 10 minutes with cardiac monitoring (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Anticonvulsants
actions: Phenobarbitone 20 mg/kg over 15 minutes; if still seizing after 15 minutes, 10 mg/kg (ICMR STW).
Then phenytoin, then lorazepam, midazolam or levetiracetam (ICMR STW).
Aim for total or near-total seizure control; monitor breathing closely (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Duration
actions: Single brief seizure with one loading dose: no maintenance (ICMR STW).
Stop other drugs after 72 hours seizure-free; stop phenobarbitone at 1 week or discharge if examination and EEG normal (ICMR STW).

teaching.scope: Neonatal seizures in Indian newborn units.
learningObjectives: Use the anticonvulsant sequence and stop drugs early.
keyPoints: Calcium gluconate 10% 2 mL/kg with cardiac monitoring.
Stop phenobarbitone at 1 week or discharge if exam and EEG normal.

lifestyleAndDiet: Breast milk; feeding plan per the baby's condition.
mdtReferrals: Paediatric neurologist if drugs needed beyond 3 months (ICMR STW)
Neonatal transport to a higher centre if needed (ICMR STW)
dischargeCriteria: Phenobarbitone stopped or maintenance plan given (ICMR STW)
